name: section-helper-load-checks
body:
Section-helper calls are static references and are checked with the rest of the template set when the resolved library is loaded (template-build-checks; templates-dir-validation step 4), from the same parsed layout trees the loader already builds. For every `{{ section "<name>" [fields] [body] [child…] }}` call in a layout: `<name>` must resolve to an existing section-usage template — an unknown name or a slide-usage template is a path-qualified templates error with a closest-match suggestion; when `fields` is present and is a literal `dict` call, every literal key must be a field the target declares, and every required field of the target must be present among those keys or carry a default; when `fields` is omitted, the target's defaults apply, so a required field of the target that carries no default is a path-qualified templates error.

Each child argument is checked at load when it is a literal `child` call: its named section must be a declared section of the target whose declaration accepts the instantiated template, its `fields` (when present and a literal `dict`) must supply every required field of the instantiated template or the required field must carry a default, and its `fields` omitted takes the instantiated template's defaults exactly as an omitted `fields` does for `section` — a required field of the child's instantiated template that carries no default is a path-qualified templates error; its literal `body` is checked against the instantiated template's body rule; and its nested `child` arguments are checked the same way, recursively. The target's children are statically known when every child argument of the call is a literal `child` call, nested `child` arguments being literal `child` calls likewise. When the target's children are statically known, the literal child set passed to a declared section satisfies that declaration's min and does not exceed its max, each violation a path-qualified templates error. A call that mixes literal `child` arguments with a `children` forwarding or any other non-literal child argument validates each literal `child` as above — accepted section, template, fields, body and nested children — and skips the target's min/max child-count checks, because the full set of children is known only when the target renders. A child argument that is not a literal `child` call — a variable, or a `children` forwarding of a `.data` list — is not inspected at load; it passes through and is checked against the target's declared sections when the target renders.

The call and every literal child template reference are reference edges of the template composition graph, so they participate in the same cycle rejection as declared sections — two section templates whose layouts call each other through the helper are rejected with the chain (requirements.constraint.section-cycle-error-chain). A `body` that is a literal string in the layout is parsed at load against the target's body rule: a heading in it that names a declared child section of the target is a path-qualified templates error (the same rejection the body rule produces when the body is validated), because children pass through child arguments, never through the body. A `body` expression that is not a literal string cannot be inspected at load; it is rejected against the target's body rule when the target renders (or its example is validated). A `fields` expression that is not a literal `dict` call — a variable, a `.raw` or `.item.parent` pass-through, or a range value — is allowed (pass-through is intended); it loads, and its keys and required fields are checked when the target renders (field-rules).

AC: a helper naming an unknown template, or a slide template, fails at load with a path-qualified templates error and a closest-match suggestion; a helper whose literal `dict` supplies a key the target does not declare fails at load naming the key; a helper omitting a required field that has no default fails at load; a literal child whose instantiated template the target's declared section does not accept fails at load; a statically known literal child set that leaves a declared section below its min (or above its max) fails at load; a call mixing literal `child` arguments with a `children` forwarding or another non-literal child argument loads, each literal child checked individually (accepted section, template, fields, body, nested children) and the target's min/max deferred to render; a `child` with omitted `fields` whose instantiated template requires a field with no default fails at load, and a `child` with omitted `fields` otherwise takes the instantiated template's defaults exactly as `section` does; a helper whose literal `body` contains a heading naming a declared child section of the target fails at load; a helper passing a non-literal `body` expression or a non-literal child argument loads, both checked when the target renders; section templates a and b whose layouts each call `{{ section "<the other>" }}` are rejected at load as a cycle whose chain names both; a helper passing a non-literal `fields` expression — a variable, a `.raw`/`.item.parent` pass-through or a range value — loads, its keys checked when the target renders.
